mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% over three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals increased consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (below 1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity is abundant.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative more than 60% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) over a quarter suggests a shift in consumer spending patterns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors reassess economic fundamentals.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases and RSAFS decreases in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where GDPC1 increased and RSAFS decreased over a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased and UNRATE decreased over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a CPI increase above 2.5% over a month during a period of economic expansion signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increased by more than 2.5% during an economic expansion.
